summary: Ernest B. Havell was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Reading School and the Royal College of Art, he served in the Indian Education Service (1885–1906) and headed art colleges in Chennai (1884–1892) and Calcutta (1896–1906).

Indologist and linguist Ernest Bender earned degrees from Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania, studying under W. Norman Brown, Henry Hoenigswald, and Zellig Harris. He taught at Penn (1946–1989) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society (1964–1988).
Ernest Clerc de Landresse was a scholar in Sinology and Japanology. He was educated at the École des chartes and studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat.

Working in philosophy, Japanology, and archaeology, Ernest Fenollosa studied at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He held teaching posts at the University of Tokyo (from 1878) and curated the Oriental Collection at Boston's Museum of Fine Arts (1890–1896).

Ernest Herbert Cooper Walsh worked in Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology after studying at Trent College and University College London. He served as Lecturer in Bengali at Oxford (1920–1921) and Lecturer in Tibetan at SOAS (~1923–1930).

Archaeologist and Indologist Ernest John Henry Mackay studied at the University of Bristol and under Flinders Petrie and John Marshall. He served as Custodian of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine (1919–1922) and Special Officer for the Archaeological Survey of India (1926–1931).
Ernest Monnington Bowden was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was educated at Malvern College (~1873–1878) and completed his B.A. at Pembroke College, Cambridge (~1878–1881).
Ernest Paxton Janvier worked in Indology and religious studies. He completed an A.B. at Princeton University (~1912–1916) and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania (~1916–1920).

Indologist Ernest Philip Horrwitz taught comparative philology at the universities of Mumbai and Rangoon. He served as Sanskrit Professor at Trinity College Dublin (~1907–1914) and Sanskrit Instructor at the City College of New York.

Ernest Renan worked in linguistics, history, and religious studies, studying at Saint-Sulpice and the Collège de France under Burnouf and Quatremère. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale (1851–1860) and the Collège de France (from 1861).

Philosopher Ernest Sosa studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as a professor at Brown University (beginning 1964) and Rutgers University (1998–2006).

Ernst Arbman was an Indologist and scholar of religion who earned his degrees at Uppsala University under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Jarl Charpentier. He was a docent at Uppsala (1922) and Professor of Comparative Religion at Stockholm University (1937–1958).
Ernst Arthur Voretzsch was a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied law at the University of Göttingen from ~1887 to 1891.

Ernst Carl Büchi worked in Indology and anthropology, studying at Zurich under Otto Schlaginhaufen and Copenhagen. He served as Superintendent at the Anthropological Survey of India (1950–1958) and Professor of Anthropology at the Free University of Berlin (1966–1979).

Philosopher Ernst Cassirer studied at Berlin and Marburg. He held posts at Berlin (~1906–1919), Hamburg (1919–1933), Oxford (1933–1935), Gothenburg (1935–1941), Yale (1941–1944), and Columbia (1944–1945).

Art historian and Indologist Ernst Cohn-Wiener studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University. He taught at the Humboldt-Akademie (~1908–1933) and directed the Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery (~1934–1939).

Archaeologist and historian Ernst Curtius studied under Friedrich Welcker and Christian Brandis at Bonn and Göttingen. He held professorships at Berlin (from 1844) and Göttingen (1855–1867), and directed the Altes Museum (~1872–1896).

Linguist Ernst Fraenkel studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Leipzig under Johannes Schmidt, Wilhelm Schulze, and August Leskien. He served as professor at Kiel University (1909–1936) and lectured at the University of Hamburg (1945–1953).

Linguist and historian Ernst Förstemann studied at Berlin and Halle under Franz Bopp, Karl Lachmann, and August Friedrich Pott. He served as a librarian at Wernigerode (from 1851) and directed the Saxon State Library in Dresden (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held positions at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), the University of Vienna (2006–2016), and the University for Continuing Education Krems.
